title: How long a grade 3 passage runs
statement: How long a grade 3 informational passage should run is unsettled: an authoring ladder sets early units well below the length a research band calls for.
example: An early review measured the course's passages at 58 to 217 words, averaging about 166.
detail: Documents in one reading course set different targets for the same kind of text. Its authoring ladder, written for the grade 3 build, puts a unit 1 informational passage at 380 to 420 words, and a grade 4 lesson plan says the ladder puts units 1 and 2 there. A grade 3 unit 2 lesson design, meanwhile, expanded its passage from 482 to 557 words to reach a research band of 520 to 560 words, citing five assessment and research sources. An early review had measured the course's passages at 58 to 217 words, averaging about 166.

evidence.quote: Our authoring ladder was written for the Grade 3 build and puts a Unit 1 informational passage at 380 to 420 words, which is the Grade 3 figure.
350 to 450 words, targeting 380 to 420. The authoring contract's length ladder puts U1 and U2 there and the informational sibling at the shorter end.

The Wonderful World of Plants was expanded from 482 to 557 words to reach the research band (520 to 560 words, 45 to 55 sentences, 10 to 12 words per sentence; NWEA, Smarter Balanced, Shanahan, STAAR, CKLA).
Course passages run 58 to 217 words, averaging about 166.
